name: Quizpio – Live Multiplayer Quizzes, Polls & Trivia
author: Quizpio

sections.description:
Live multiplayer quizzes, polls, and trivia inside your own WordPress site. Quizpio brings the fast-paced, PIN-to-join, shared-leaderboard kind of game you’ve seen at conferences and classrooms to WordPress — with no third-party service and no external data dependency. Players join from any device by entering a PIN and a nickname.

Built for classrooms, trainings, and audience engagement

Teachers running classroom warm-ups or end-of-unit reviews. Trainers running team-building sessions. Course creators making lessons interactive. Membership site owners driving engagement. Trivia night hosts at bars and community centers. Event organizers wanting an audience-engagement moment. Anyone who wants a real-time shared-screen game that runs in a browser, on the site they already own.

Let multiple people run their own quizzes

Running a site where more than one person makes quizzes — a few teachers sharing a school site, or several colleagues each hosting their own sessions? Assign the Quizpio Quiz Author role and each author can create, edit, and host their own quizzes from the dashboard. Authors see only their own sessions, results, and CSV exports, and can delete the sessions they ran; administrators see everything across the site. Assigning the role is all it takes, unless another plugin restricts dashboard access (see the FAQ).

Build quizzes and polls with Gutenberg blocks

Each quiz is its own custom post type with its own URL, so you manage quizzes like Posts or Pages. Inside, you compose questions using the standard Gutenberg editor — multiple-choice (4 options) or true/false. Every question has its own time limit and point value, and any question can be switched to a poll — no points, no correct answer — for opinion checks and icebreakers mixed right into the game. As you build, the editor checks each question — prompting you for the question text, a second option, unique options, and a marked correct answer (polls skip that last one) — so every published quiz is ready to play. Every quiz has a settings panel where you choose:

  • Scoring style — Speed bonus (faster correct answers earn more, scaling from 50% to 100% of max) or Flat (every correct answer earns the full value, the right choice for assessments where speed shouldn’t matter).
  • Reveal answers between questions — show or skip the reveal screen that displays the correct answer and live vote distribution.
  • Show full standings to players — let players see the complete leaderboard on Final Results, or just the top 10 plus their own rank.
  • Require host to click Next between questions — switch from auto-advance to manual pacing for classroom discussion or debrief moments.
  • Let players share their result — a Share button on each player’s Final Results. On phones and tablets it opens the share options; on computers it copies the result. On by default.

Want the quiz inside an existing post or page instead of at its own URL? Drop in a Quizpio Quiz Embed block, pick a quiz from the dropdown, publish. Same quiz, played at that location. Sessions still belong to the quiz itself, so results from embedded plays roll up to one quiz history.

The live host and player experience

For the host: Open the quiz at its own URL (or the post where you embedded it). Hit Launch Session. Share the PIN. Watch the player list fill up, then hit Start Quiz. A brief “Get ready!” countdown brings everyone to the first question at the same moment. Each question then shows for a few seconds before answering opens, so every screen has it — even on a slow connection — before anyone’s clock starts. Run the quiz with live controls — start, skip, pause, resume, end — and a sidebar leaderboard that updates in real time. Wide screens get the leaderboard next to the question; phones stack it below. Each reveal screen shows the correct answer, how many players picked each option, and the standings going into the next question. On a poll question there is no correct answer to reveal — the screen shows how the room voted, and the summary reports a response rate rather than an accuracy figure.

For the player: Visit the quiz page on any device — phone, tablet, or laptop. Enter the PIN, pick a nickname (or have it prefilled from your WordPress profile if you’re logged in), and you’re in. You get a color avatar generated deterministically from your nickname, so you have a visual identity that recurs across sessions. Read each question as it appears, and tap your answer when answering opens a few seconds later. Watch your score climb. Poll questions are tagged as polls on your own screen, so you always know when an answer isn’t being scored. The leaderboard always shows your own row — even when you’re outside the top — with a YOU badge so you always know where you stand. Need to step away? Tap Leave; you exit cleanly without breaking the session for everyone else.

At the end: A Final Results screen with a top-3 medal-card podium, summary stats, the full standings (if enabled), a per-question accuracy recap, and a “Held on” byline showing the date, time, and duration — for example, “May 17, 2026 · 2:30 PM – 2:42 PM EDT · 12 min” — rendered in each viewer’s local timezone via the browser’s Intl API. Top-3 finishers get a confetti burst on their own screen, and the host’s results screen celebrates too — all respecting prefers-reduced-motion. Each player can share their own result, with a link to the quiz page. If every question in the quiz was a poll, the finish is survey-style instead: response rates and vote distributions, with no scores and no podium.

Guests vs. logged-in players: Guest play with just a nickname works by default — no account creation, no friction. Logged-in WordPress users get a richer experience: their nickname prefills from their profile, a “My past plays” button on the join and Final Results screens opens a personal history of every session they’ve played on this site, and they appear on the Players screen in the WordPress admin, where site owners can see who’s been playing across sessions. Both tiers play the same quiz; you choose whether to require accounts via a single setting.

On refreshes and reconnects: Players who refresh, lose connection, or close the tab can rejoin and land back in the live session as it currently stands — same identity and score, and if they’d already answered the question on screen, their answer is still locked in with its result shown. Identity persists in the browser’s local storage for up to 6 hours or until that session ends. The host’s view survives refresh too.

Accessible and theme-independent

Quizpio is keyboard-navigable throughout, with ARIA roles and live regions so screen readers announce each phase change. The quiz interface carries its own styling and behavior rather than inheriting from the active theme, so it never picks up a theme’s fonts or layout quirks and works the same on every site. It renders in your device’s native system font, so type looks at home on Mac, Windows, or Android. All motion effects, the confetti included, respect the visitor’s reduced-motion preference.

Admin tools, when you want them

A dashboard with stats and an active-session callout with a one-click “Open host view.” A Sessions screen with filtering by quiz, pagination, and per-session detail showing the leaderboard plus a per-question breakdown with answer distribution, and an administrator can force-end an abandoned session from that detail page, or download a support file for it — the session’s data, its event log, a record of quiz edits around it and the site’s software versions, to send to Quizpio support. A CSV export with Nickname, Rank, Score, Question #, Question text, Selected Option, Correct Answer, Correct?, Points, response-time-in-milliseconds, Answered at, Joined at and Quizpio version per row — filename carries the quiz slug plus the session’s launch date, time and number, so downloads stay sortable and never collide in a teacher’s Downloads folder. For sites with returning players, the Players screen lists registered users with sessions-played, best score, last played, and click-through to a per-user history. Site-wide Settings cover polling interval (responsiveness vs. server load tradeoff), reveal pause duration, and a guest-allow toggle, plus manual data cleanup — delete sessions by date range, or wipe all session data. Quizpio never deletes anything on its own.

Free to use, with an optional Pro add-on

GPL v2, open source, and complete on its own. No feature of the free plugin is held back for the paid add-on, now or later — no feature locks, and nothing that interrupts you: no dashboard banners, no upgrade nags, nothing pushed at you that you did not ask for. There is one page under the Quizpio menu describing Quizpio Pro, and it disappears once Pro is active. Runs on any standard WordPress host — no Node.js, no WebSocket server, no third-party service required. Translation-ready with a bundled .pot file. Deleting Quizpio removes all of its data — tables, options, quizzes, and session results — for a clean uninstall, with a setting to keep everything instead — quizzes, results, and settings — if you plan to reinstall later.

What Quizpio Pro adds

Quizpio Pro is a separate paid add-on, sold as a yearly license on the quizpio.com website. It installs alongside this plugin and adds to it — none of the features above depend on it.

  • AI quiz generation — one click with an AI provider, or paste the prompt into any AI chat
  • Question and answer images — pictures on questions and on individual options
  • Rank-change animation — the host leaderboard shows who climbed and who fell
  • Streak bonus and double points — reward consecutive correct answers
  • Certificates — every player downloads one, with your logo and signature
  • Scan to join — a lobby QR code players scan instead of typing your site address
  • Guided setup — a one-screen wizard for installing and updating
sections.installation:
From your WordPress dashboard (recommended):

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New and search for “Quizpio”.
  2. Click Install Now, then Activate.

Or install manually:

  1. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin, choose quizpio.zip, click Install Now, then Activate.
  2. Or via FTP: extract quizpio to /wp-content/plugins/ and activate it from the Plugins page.

Then create your first quiz:

  1. Open Quizpio in your admin sidebar to review settings.
  2. Click Quizpio → Add New Quiz, add a title, drop in some Question blocks, and publish.
  3. Visit the quiz URL to host it (or click the quiz title in the Quizzes list to edit, then View on its row).
sections.faq:
How is Quizpio different from other WordPress quiz plugins?

Most WordPress quiz plugins are static — a user opens a page, answers questions in a form, sees their score. Quizpio is live and multiplayer: everyone plays at the same time, scores update in real time on a shared leaderboard, and the host runs the session from the same page players see. The mental model is closer to the live-poll tools you’ve seen at conferences or classrooms than to a typical form-based quiz.

Can several teachers or staff each run their own quizzes?

Yes. Assign someone the Quizpio Quiz Author role (in Users → add or edit a user → Role) and they can create, edit, and host their own quizzes. Each author sees only the sessions and results from quizzes they host — administrators see all of them. It’s a good fit for a school site shared by several teachers, or any organization where more than one person runs quizzes.

My Quiz Author is sent to the home page or the My Account page instead of the dashboard. What do I do?

Some shop and membership plugins keep users out of the WordPress dashboard unless their role is allowed, and the Quizpio Quiz Author role is new to them. Quizpio already lets Quiz Authors past WooCommerce’s check. For any other plugin, allow the Quizpio Quiz Author role in that plugin’s settings. In Ultimate Member, go to Ultimate Member → User Roles, edit Quizpio Quiz Author, turn on Can access wp-admin?, turn off Force hiding adminbar in frontend? so they keep the toolbar, and save. Creating and editing quizzes and reviewing past sessions need the dashboard; hosting happens on the quiz’s own page.

Can I use Quizpio for remote or virtual classes?

Yes. Players join from any device with a PIN, and the host shares the question screen over your usual video call, so Quizpio works for remote and virtual classes the same way it does in a room together. Students answer on their own phones or laptops while everyone watches the live leaderboard — nothing extra for them to install, just a browser.

Is Quizpio good for gamified learning or e-learning?

Yes. Live points, the speed bonus, and a shared leaderboard bring game mechanics — gamification — to lessons and online courses, turning review and practice into something students want to win. Embed a quiz inside a course or e-learning page with the Quizpio Quiz Embed block, run it live during a session, and the competitive feedback loop does the engagement work.

Will this work on my shared hosting?

Yes. No Node.js, no WebSocket server, no external service. Pure WordPress with REST polling — updates appear within ~2 seconds. Tested with a room of 100 players on a small host with 4 PHP workers.

Does Quizpio support WordPress multisite?

Quizpio is designed for single-site installs. It runs fine when activated on an individual subsite, but network-wide activation isn’t supported — activate it per site.

Does Quizpio work with page-cache plugins (WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, LiteSpeed Cache, etc.)?

Yes. Quizpio sends explicit no-store headers on its REST endpoints, defines DONOTCACHEPAGE during each request, and appends a cache-busting query parameter on every poll. That combination protects against nearly all real-world cache-plugin configurations. If you’re still seeing players stuck on a stale view, exclude /wp-json/quizpio/* from your cache plugin’s URL rules as a final defensive measure.

Does Quizpio work with the Classic Editor plugin?

Yes, Quizpio still works when the Classic Editor plugin is active. Quizzes are built in the block editor (Gutenberg), so Quizpio always opens quizzes there, even when Classic Editor or Disable Gutenberg is active. Your posts and pages keep whichever editor you choose — Quizpio doesn’t change that.

If the quiz builder still doesn’t appear, another plugin is blocking the block editor in a different way. Deactivate your plugins one at a time to find it, and let us know which one.

Is there a paid version?

Yes. Quizpio Pro is a separate paid add-on, sold as a yearly license on the quizpio.com website. It installs alongside this plugin rather than replacing it, and no feature of the free plugin is held back for it — Pro adds to it rather than unlocking it. The free plugin contains no feature locks and nothing that interrupts you; one page under the Quizpio menu describes what Pro adds, and it disappears once Pro is active.

Do players need an account?

No — guest play with just a nickname works by default. Logged-in WordPress users get extras: their nickname prefills from their profile, and a “My past plays” button gives them a personal history of their results across sessions. If you want to require accounts, flip the “Allow guest players” setting off.

How many players can join a single quiz?

There’s no fixed cap — it scales with your host. In our tests, a small host with 4 PHP workers ran a room of 100 players smoothly. On a slow, overloaded host, where every request took over a second, rooms of up to 35 stayed on time; bigger rooms fell behind. Since the plugin works by having each player’s browser poll the server, the real ceiling is how many of those requests your host can serve, not a number baked into Quizpio.

Can I configure how quizzes behave?

Yes. Each quiz has its own settings in the Gutenberg editor sidebar: scoring style (speed bonus or flat), whether to show reveal screens between questions, whether players see the full leaderboard at the end, whether the host must click Next between questions (manual mode for classroom discussion), and whether players can share their result. Site-wide, you can adjust how often players’ browsers poll the server and how long reveal screens last.

Can I export quiz results?

Yes. Quizpio → Sessions → click any session → Export CSV — or click Download CSV right on the final-results screen after hosting a game. The CSV includes nickname, rank, score, per-answer detail with the selected option and the correct answer, points awarded, response time in milliseconds, when each answer arrived, when each player joined, and the Quizpio version the session ran on.

What question types does Quizpio support?

Multiple-choice (4 options) and true/false. Both are authored in the same Question block — switch between them via the Type setting in the block sidebar. The two True/False labels are ordinary answer options, so you can rename them — useful when your quiz is written in a language other than your site’s. Either type can become a poll with the Poll — no points toggle.

How is scoring calculated?

Each quiz has a Scoring style setting. Speed bonus (default) gives faster correct answers more points — between 50% and 100% of the question’s max. Flat gives every correct answer the full point value regardless of speed, which is the better fit for assessments.

What happens if a player refreshes their browser?

They stay in the quiz. Player identity is stored in the browser’s local storage and persists across refreshes for up to 6 hours, or until that quiz session ends.

Can I run two quizzes on the same page?

No. Only one quiz can run per page — that means one Quizpio Quiz Embed block per post or page. If a second one is added by mistake, it is disabled automatically and shows a short notice in its place, so the first quiz keeps working. (You can run different quizzes on different posts, of course.)

Can players leave a quiz once it has started?

Yes. A Leave link appears on every question and reveal screen. After a confirmation prompt, the player exits the quiz cleanly. Any score they’ve already earned stays on the leaderboard, but they can’t rejoin that same session. (Players still in the lobby leave fully — their entry is removed.)

Will I see my rank if I’m not in the top players?

Yes. The leaderboard shows the top 5 on the reveal after each scored question and the top 10 on the final results screen. If you finish outside those cuts, your row appears below the list (after a “…” separator) with a YOU badge, so you always know where you stand.

How do I run a poll or opinion question?

Switch on Poll — no points in the question’s block settings. Poll questions have no correct answer and award no points; the reveal shows how the group voted, with no leaderboard, since a poll changes nobody’s score (with the quiz’s reveal setting on, everyone sees the vote split after each poll; with it off, nobody sees it during the game; your final results screen shows each poll’s top pick, and Quizpio → Sessions shows every vote). If every question in a quiz is a poll, players get a survey-style finish with no scores or podium, and the quiz’s scoring settings hide in the editor. The old workaround — setting Max points to 0 — no longer works: those questions now score normally, so switch them to polls.

How do I translate Quizpio?

The plugin ships with a quizpio.pot file in the languages/ folder. Use Poedit or Loco Translate to create translations and place the resulting .po/.mo files in wp-content/languages/plugins/.

Some text on the live quiz screens is rendered by JavaScript rather than PHP — the counted labels in particular, so that each language can apply its own plural rules. WordPress loads those from .json files rather than .mo, generated with wp i18n make-json. Translating on translate.wordpress.org handles this for you; translating locally, it is the step that is easy to miss, and the symptom is a handful of labels staying in English while everything else translates.

Where can I report bugs or request features?

https://quizpio.com/contact/
sections.changelog:
1.3.6

  • Added: Players can share their result from the Final Results screen. On phones and tablets, Share Result opens the device’s share options; on computers, it copies the result. It shares only the player’s own rank and score (for a poll, that they took part) and a link to the page they played on, and it shows only while that page is public. Hosts can turn it off for any quiz in Quiz Settings.
  • Fixed: Final Results now opens at its top, even when the player had scrolled down to answer the last question.
  • Fixed: A player’s screen no longer jumps back to an earlier question when the site briefly serves out-of-date session data; it follows a real change only when the data stays that way.
  • Fixed: When the site is briefly behind a player’s screen, the answer is sent again until it counts, instead of being refused at once. If the question closes first, the screen says the answer couldn’t be saved.
  • Fixed: A player is no longer signed out of a running game by a single rejected request, and a signed-in player whose WordPress login ends mid-quiz keeps playing.
  • Fixed: An answer the site refused is shown in a neutral style, not as a wrong answer.
  • Fixed: Pressing Start twice on an out-of-date screen can no longer restart a running quiz.
  • Fixed: Guests can join from a quiz page that a page cache has kept for more than a day. Such a page carried an expired security token, and joining failed with “Cookie check failed”.
  • Added: Each session records the Quizpio, WordPress and PHP versions it ran on, and its CSV export gains three columns at the end: Answered at, Joined at and Quizpio version.
  • Added: A per-session event log for support: when each question opened and closed, pauses, the end, and every answer or player token the site refused, with what the site believed at that moment. Never addresses, emails or tokens.
  • Added: A record of quiz edits around a session: edits that reached it at Start, edits saved while it ran, and the quiz as it is now.
  • Added: A “Download Support File” button on a session’s page, for administrators only: one file with the session’s data, its log, the edit record and the site’s software versions, to send to Quizpio support when something went wrong.
  • Fixed: On touch screens, a tapped answer’s spot no longer stays highlighted on the next question, where it could look already chosen.
  • Fixed: The quiz editor no longer logs a deprecation notice in the browser console on WordPress 6.6 and later.
  • Improved: Player names get more room on narrow screens.

1.3.5

  • Fixed: Data & Cleanup now keeps sessions that are still in progress, so it’s safe to tidy up old data at any time. Its confirmation shows exactly how many sessions will be deleted.
  • Fixed: Reinstalling Quizpio after deleting it now sets everything up again, so nicknames stay unique even when two players join at the same moment. Sites that reinstalled on an earlier version get this back when they update.
  • Fixed: Updates now always finish setting up the Quiz Author role, even if the first page load after an update is cut short.
  • Fixed: Changing your site’s time zone no longer shifts the times of past sessions on Final Results, My Past Plays and the admin screens.
  • Improved: When a busy site asks a player to tap again but their first answer was saved after all, their screen now says so: “Your first answer was saved.”
  • Improved: Big rooms are easier to follow. With more than 20 players, the final leaderboards show the top places first, with “Show All” for everyone, and the admin session page lists 50 players per page.
  • Improved: The question recap on the host’s final screen folds back with “Show Less” and reads better on small screens.
  • Improved: My Past Plays shows a quiz made only of polls as “Poll” instead of a score of 0.

1.3.4

  • Fixed: On busy sites, a player could be asked to tap again although their answer had been saved, and the reveal then said “No answer”. The phone now waits for a slow reply, sends an answer again only when it seems lost, never asks for a new tap once time is up, and the reveal shows the answer the quiz saved.

1.3.3

  • Fixed: On slower sites, questions could reach players’ screens late, with some of the answering time already gone. Each question now shows for a few seconds before answering opens — the timer counts down “Answers open in…” — so every screen has it in time and starts with the full time.
  • Fixed: Speed points no longer include the time your site takes to respond. Answers are timed from when they reach the server.
  • Fixed: An answer tapped in the last second could be refused with “No active question.” and no feedback afterwards. Answers already on their way now get 3 extra seconds to arrive, and one that is still too late is told so on the reveal.
  • Fixed: Edits you save while a quiz’s lobby is open now reach that session when you press Start Quiz. Before, the session kept the copy taken at Launch Session, so a corrected answer could still mark right answers wrong.
  • Fixed: Add New Quiz and editing a quiz always open the block editor, even with the Classic Editor or Disable Gutenberg plugin active, so the quiz builder is always there. Posts and pages keep the editor you choose — Quizpio doesn’t change that.
  • Fixed: If the host paused just as a player tapped an answer, that player could not answer the question after the quiz resumed. Now they see a note to tap again, and the new answer counts.
  • Fixed: When a connection or server problem stopped a player’s answer from reaching the quiz, their device showed “Incorrect” and locked the answers, even for a correct answer. Now the device resends the answer automatically, and if it still can’t get through, asks the player to tap again.
  • Fixed: A firewall or CDN error page, such as a rate-limit check, could sign a player out of a running quiz with no way back in. Players now stay in, and their device keeps reconnecting.
  • Improved: The Background Refresh Interval setting now explains how it sets the length of each question’s lead-in.

1.3.2

  • Fixed: Every player’s final screen now shows their true place in the room, e.g. “You finished #12 of 28”.
  • Improved: CSV exports now include the session’s date, time and number in the filename, so same-day sessions never share a name.
  • Improved: Clearer first-run steps on the Quizpio dashboard and Welcome screen, and more accurate examples in the plugin description.

1.3.1

  • Fixed: On sites running WooCommerce, users with the Quizpio Quiz Author role were sent to the My Account page instead of the dashboard and lost the toolbar on the front end, so they couldn’t create or manage their quizzes. They now reach Quizpio’s screens and keep the toolbar as intended.

1.3.0

  • Fixed: After a poll question, the reveal could still show a leaderboard — on players’ screens in a mixed quiz, and on the host’s screen with the side panel hidden. A poll question changes nobody’s score, so its reveal now shows only the votes, everywhere. Scored questions keep their leaderboard.
  • Improved: In an all-poll quiz, the host’s side-panel button now reads “Hide Players” / “Show Players” — that panel lists players, not a leaderboard.
  • Improved: In an all-poll quiz, the editor’s Quiz Settings panel hides Scoring style and Show full standings, which don’t apply to polls. Nothing is lost — switch any question back to scored and both return exactly as you left them.
  • Added: Each button in the host’s action bar now carries a stable name (data-qp-action), so add-ons can place their own buttons reliably. Nothing changes for hosts.

1.2.1

  • Fixed: Joining could rarely appear to succeed without adding the player — they’d land in the quiz unable to answer. It now fails clearly and can be retried.
  • Fixed: Two players claiming the same nickname at the same instant could both join, leaving two identical names on the leaderboard.
  • Improved: Dropped a redundant index on the answers table — one less write per answer.
  • Note: Updates Quizpio’s database tables, automatically, on upgrade.

1.2.0

  • Fixed: The live quiz now uses WordPress’s current rendering method, so it keeps working on future WordPress releases. Nothing about how you build or host a quiz changes.
  • Fixed: Counts and their labels now agree — a finish screen with one question reads “1 Question”, not “1 Questions”. Each language uses its own plural rules.
  • Fixed: The Settings page now confirms when your settings have been saved. They always were; there was simply no message saying so.
  • Added: A Quizpio Pro page under the Quizpio menu, describing the optional paid add-on. It is one page you can ignore — nothing else in the plugin mentions it, and it disappears entirely once Quizpio Pro is active.

1.1.0

New

  • Poll questions — switch any question to Poll — no points. No correct answer, nothing scored; the reveal shows how the group voted. An all-poll quiz gets a survey-style finish instead of a podium.
  • Quiz Author role — give teachers or colleagues their own access to create and host quizzes. Each author sees only their own sessions and results; administrators still see everything.
  • Editable True/False labels — rename them to run True/False questions in any language.
  • Pre-start countdown — a short “Get ready!” on the host and player screens, so everyone starts together.
  • Editor completion checks — an incomplete question is flagged before you publish (no prompt, fewer than two options, duplicate options, no correct answer marked), with the missing pieces listed inline. Drafts always save; only publishing is blocked.
  • Admin force-end — administrators can end any running session to clear an abandoned lobby or game.
  • Delete sessions by date range, not just before a single date.
  • Choose what happens on uninstall — remove everything (the default), or keep everything — quizzes, results, and settings — for a future reinstall.

Improved

  • Session privacy — rosters, final standings, and question recaps are no longer readable by outsiders who guess a session address, and players now authenticate their live updates with their session token. If you update while a session is running, host and players should refresh once.
  • Accessibility — keyboard focus follows each new question, and dialogs keep focus inside.
  • The Time limit and Max points fields show their allowed ranges.

Fixed

  • Stability and interface fixes across the host and player screens — REST requests on every permalink setting, session restore and reconnect, countdown accuracy, leaderboard and scoring edge cases, and a more thorough uninstall.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.

  • Reveal answers between questions — show or skip the reveal screen that displays the correct answer and live vote distribution.
  • Show full standings to players — let players see the complete leaderboard on Final Results, or just the top 10 plus their own rank.
  • Require host to click Next between questions — switch from auto-advance to manual pacing for classroom discussion or debrief moments.
  • Let players share their result — a Share button on each player’s Final Results. On phones and tablets it opens the share options; on computers it copies the result. On by default.

Want the quiz inside an existing post or page instead of at its own URL? Drop in a Quizpio Quiz Embed block, pick a quiz from the dropdown, publish. Same quiz, played at that location. Sessions still belong to the quiz itself, so results from embedded plays roll up to one quiz history.

The live host and player experience

For the host: Open the quiz at its own URL (or the post where you embedded it). Hit Launch Session. Share the PIN. Watch the player list fill up, then hit Start Quiz. A brief “Get ready!” countdown brings everyone to the first question at the same moment. Each question then shows for a few seconds before answering opens, so every screen has it — even on a slow connection — before anyone’s clock starts. Run the quiz with live controls — start, skip, pause, resume, end — and a sidebar leaderboard that updates in real time. Wide screens get the leaderboard next to the question; phones stack it below. Each reveal screen shows the correct answer, how many players picked each option, and the standings going into the next question. On a poll question there is no correct answer to reveal — the screen shows how the room voted, and the summary reports a response rate rather than an accuracy figure.

For the player: Visit the quiz page on any device — phone, tablet, or laptop. Enter the PIN, pick a nickname (or have it prefilled from your WordPress profile if you’re logged in), and you’re in. You get a color avatar generated deterministically from your nickname, so you have a visual identity that recurs across sessions. Read each question as it appears, and tap your answer when answering opens a few seconds later. Watch your score climb. Poll questions are tagged as polls on your own screen, so you always know when an answer isn’t being scored. The leaderboard always shows your own row — even when you’re outside the top — with a YOU badge so you always know where you stand. Need to step away? Tap Leave; you exit cleanly without breaking the session for everyone else.

At the end: A Final Results screen with a top-3 medal-card podium, summary stats, the full standings (if enabled), a per-question accuracy recap, and a “Held on” byline showing the date, time, and duration — for example, “May 17, 2026 · 2:30 PM – 2:42 PM EDT · 12 min” — rendered in each viewer’s local timezone via the browser’s Intl API. Top-3 finishers get a confetti burst on their own screen, and the host’s results screen celebrates too — all respecting prefers-reduced-motion. Each player can share their own result, with a link to the quiz page. If every question in the quiz was a poll, the finish is survey-style instead: response rates and vote distributions, with no scores and no podium.

Guests vs. logged-in players: Guest play with just a nickname works by default — no account creation, no friction. Logged-in WordPress users get a richer experience: their nickname prefills from their profile, a “My past plays” button on the join and Final Results screens opens a personal history of every session they’ve played on this site, and they appear on the Players screen in the WordPress admin, where site owners can see who’s been playing across sessions. Both tiers play the same quiz; you choose whether to require accounts via a single setting.

On refreshes and reconnects: Players who refresh, lose connection, or close the tab can rejoin and land back in the live session as it currently stands — same identity and score, and if they’d already answered the question on screen, their answer is still locked in with its result shown. Identity persists in the browser’s local storage for up to 6 hours or until that session ends. The host’s view survives refresh too.

Accessible and theme-independent

Quizpio is keyboard-navigable throughout, with ARIA roles and live regions so screen readers announce each phase change. The quiz interface carries its own styling and behavior rather than inheriting from the active theme, so it never picks up a theme’s fonts or layout quirks and works the same on every site. It renders in your device’s native system font, so type looks at home on Mac, Windows, or Android. All motion effects, the confetti included, respect the visitor’s reduced-motion preference.

Admin tools, when you want them

A dashboard with stats and an active-session callout with a one-click “Open host view.” A Sessions screen with filtering by quiz, pagination, and per-session detail showing the leaderboard plus a per-question breakdown with answer distribution, and an administrator can force-end an abandoned session from that detail page, or download a support file for it — the session’s data, its event log, a record of quiz edits around it and the site’s software versions, to send to Quizpio support. A CSV export with Nickname, Rank, Score, Question #, Question text, Selected Option, Correct Answer, Correct?, Points, response-time-in-milliseconds, Answered at, Joined at and Quizpio version per row — filename carries the quiz slug plus the session’s launch date, time and number, so downloads stay sortable and never collide in a teacher’s Downloads folder. For sites with returning players, the Players screen lists registered users with sessions-played, best score, last played, and click-through to a per-user history. Site-wide Settings cover polling interval (responsiveness vs. server load tradeoff), reveal pause duration, and a guest-allow toggle, plus manual data cleanup — delete sessions by date range, or wipe all session data. Quizpio never deletes anything on its own.

Free to use, with an optional Pro add-on

GPL v2, open source, and complete on its own. No feature of the free plugin is held back for the paid add-on, now or later — no feature locks, and nothing that interrupts you: no dashboard banners, no upgrade nags, nothing pushed at you that you did not ask for. There is one page under the Quizpio menu describing Quizpio Pro, and it disappears once Pro is active. Runs on any standard WordPress host — no Node.js, no WebSocket server, no third-party service required. Translation-ready with a bundled .pot file. Deleting Quizpio removes all of its data — tables, options, quizzes, and session results — for a clean uninstall, with a setting to keep everything instead — quizzes, results, and settings — if you plan to reinstall later.

What Quizpio Pro adds

Quizpio Pro is a separate paid add-on, sold as a yearly license on the quizpio.com website. It installs alongside this plugin and adds to it — none of the features above depend on it.

  • AI quiz generation — one click with an AI provider, or paste the prompt into any AI chat
  • Question and answer images — pictures on questions and on individual options
  • Rank-change animation — the host leaderboard shows who climbed and who fell
  • Streak bonus and double points — reward consecutive correct answers
  • Certificates — every player downloads one, with your logo and signature
  • Scan to join — a lobby QR code players scan instead of typing your site address
  • Guided setup — a one-screen wizard for installing and updating
